column2: How do I find the heirs of a deceased person for a notary (⚖️ probate genealogist)?
column3: Turn on the “⚖️ Probate genealogist” use (Settings → Appearance → 🧭 How you use the app): the “⚖️ Estates” tab appears. Open one file per deceased there (also: Lists → Research and organisation → “⚖️ Estate files”, or ⋯ on the deceased’s record → “⚖️ Search for the heirs…”). The file keeps the instructing notary, their reference, deadlines, the heirs and their shares, the devolution tree, the documents for each link (in hand, requested, missing), letters to the heirs and a log of every action. At the top of the tab, three buttons: “Files”, “Heirs to contact” (the living heirs of all open files, with address, contact status, ✉️ Write and CSV export) and “Letters” (only the letters of estate files, with answer and signature).

column2: How does the app calculate the heirs’ shares (devolution)?
column3: From the records, under today’s French Civil Code (art. 731 and following, to read on legifrance.gouv.fr; in the file, each article cited is a link): the surviving spouse first, then the first of the 4 orders that has someone (children; parents, brothers and sisters; other ascendants; uncles and cousins up to the 6th degree), with representation and the split between paternal and maternal branches. Shares are exact fractions. If it is not known whether an heir was alive, the app also shows the other hypothesis. The calculation is indicative: the notary checks it. For a death before July 2002, a warning says so: the law at the time was different.

column2: Do estate files leave the app?
column3: No: living heirs, their addresses and their shares stay in the file. Only the papers you make yourself leave it (table for the notary, letters, CSV export of the heirs to contact). No export (GEDCOM, Geneanet, website, sharing with the family, book) reads them, and viewing mode and simple mode do not show them. A closed file can be archived: addresses are removed, the log remains.

column2: Where should estate files go: in my family tree or separately?
column3: At the first “＋ Open a file”, the app asks: in this family tree, in a separate family tree for all your files (“⚖️ Estate files”, in 🌳 My family trees), or one family tree per file. You can change your mind in Settings → Appearance → 🧭 How you use the app → “⚖️ Where to keep the files”, where “⇄ Move…” puts a file elsewhere (both family trees are backed up first). For the deceased, “⤓ Take the record from My family tree” copies the record up to the grandparents and all their known descendants, without photos.

column2: How do I show only one estate file across the whole app (⚖️ button)?
column3: The ⚖️ button at the top right (probate use only): “Show all”, one file or several. A yellow banner reminds you; ✕ shows everything again. People, search, lists and the map show only the file’s records; in the tree, the others are greyed out without a name (or hidden: setting). A record created during the filter is linked to the file automatically, with “↶ Undo”. The Dashboard and Settings are never filtered.

column2: How do I link a person to an estate file, with a role?
column3: The deceased is linked when the file is opened, heirs and intermediaries by the calculation (a record removed by hand is never put back automatically). On a record, ⋯ → “⚖️ Files…”: one role per file (deceased, heir, intermediary, witness, to check). In the file, the “🧑‍🤝‍🧑 People” tab shows all its records. The record’s “⚖️ 2 files” badge lists its files; two records from different files you want to merge, or a namesake in another file, are flagged first.

column2: How do I see the progress of all my estate files?
column3: ⚖️ Estates → “Files”: a dashboard of all files, even those kept in another family tree (state, notary, next deadline, heirs, documents, time, progress). Tick files for “⚖️ Show only these” or a CSV export. The Dashboard widget “⚖️ My estate files” sums it up. Progress counts 7 weighted steps (deceased and record, tree, heirs found, addresses, signed contracts, documents, handed to the notary): the weights are set in Settings → Appearance → 🧭 How you use the app.

column2: How do I archive a closed estate file to a file, then re-import it?
column3: Closed file → ⋯ → “🗄 Archive to a file and remove…”: a .lcnda-succ.zip file keeps the file, the log, the documents, the letters, the tree and the records (addresses of the living kept or removed, your choice). Then the records used only by this file are removed from the database (backup first). Later: ⚖️ Estates → “⤒ Re-import an archived file…”; a record that looks like one already there is offered for comparison, never merged automatically.

column2: How do I see people grouped by estate file?
column3: 👤 People → left column → “⚖️ By file” (when the family tree has files): one collapsible folder per estate, its records from A to Z, and “No file” collapsed at the end. Files are ordered A → Z or by hand (drag ⠿, or Alt + ↑ / ↓ on the file, with “↶ Undo”). “Current view” goes back to the usual list.

column2: Do confidential records count as heirs in an estate file?
column3: Yes, by default: for the calculation, a confidential record (🔒) is a person like any other. Settings → Appearance → 🧭 How you use the app → “⚙️ File settings” → “Do confidential records count as heirs?” → No: they are removed from the calculation, as if they did not exist (never the deceased). The 👥 Heirs tab then says so (“2 confidential records not counted: the shares may be wrong”), with a link to this setting.

column2: An heir is untraceable or not responding: how do I note it in an estate file?
column3: In the file, 👥 Heirs tab (or ⚖️ Estates → “Heirs to contact”), the “Contact” menu on their row: “🔎 Untraceable” or “🔇 Not responding”, dated. The ⚖️ badge on their record shows it (“⚖️ 2026-014 · 🔇 not responding”), and ⋯ on the record → “⚖️ Files…” changes it too. Each change goes to the file’s log, with “↶ Undo”. They do not count as contacted in the progress, and the shares do not change: this is not the “Presumed absent” status. Untraceable for over a year: the app suggests “❔ Absent or missing”, which explains the presumption of absence (French Civil Code, art. 112 et seq., on legifrance.gouv.fr).

column2: I have a doubt about the law: how do I find the right article?
column3: ⚖️ Estates → “⚖️ Unsure about the law?” (or, in an open file, “⚖️ Unsure?”): write your problem in your own words, for example “deadline to renounce an estate”, then “🏛 Search on Service-public” (explains in plain French and gives the link to the right article) or “📜 Search on Légifrance” (the articles of the codes in force). The app chooses no article and writes no legal text: your question is sent as is to the official website, which opens in your browser. Don’t write any names: the question goes out on the internet. In a file, “✍️ Note in the file” keeps the question in the log, with the article’s link if you paste it (only Légifrance, Service-public or EUR-Lex).
